Tram catenary wires and platform height/guardrails match German tram/Stadtbahn infrastructure. These collectively indicate Germany and rule out neighboring countries with different bus-stop branding or sign typography.
City level: The presence of both heavy rail (multiple tracks and station canopies) and Stadtbahn/tram platforms immediately outside a central station labeled “Hauptbahnhof” narrows to large German cities. The tall disc-shaped “mushroom” streetlights, glass-canopied raised light-rail platforms, extensive bike parking, and a streetscape bending around the station plaza are characteristic of Stuttgart’s Arnulf-Klett-Platz in front of Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof. The white-on-blue “U” (Stadtbahn) symbol is also used in Stuttgart. The nearby C&A signage and station-side retail match that frontage; Berlin and Munich Hbf front plazas have different lamp designs and platform layouts, making them less consistent.
Street level: The curved roadway skirting the front of the station with bollards-and-chain edging, the paired glass stairways down to the Stadtbahn platforms on the right, clustered bike racks behind a verge, and the line of mushroom-top lamp poles center-left are distinctive to the immediate approach roads at Arnulf-Klett-Platz outside Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof. The configuration of bus stop totems on the left and taxi/parking signs on the right further pin the specific frontage segment of the plaza.
Putting these together, the most plausible location is Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, at or near Arnulf-Klett-Platz by Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof.
